resources.string: The order and the opening section are the same on every server. The switches are for this server only.
The server refused this key. Nothing is known yet about what runs on it.
The server could not be reached. This says nothing about the agent.
The server answered, but nothing there speaks as the gryonixNexus agent.
The agent is there and refused a step.

Some of these were already on this server. gryonixNexus manages what it installed itself — to manage one of them from here, back its data up, remove it on the machine, and install it again from the app.
Passwords are kept behind the device keystore, never in the fleet file.
Trust a new host key on the next connection
The next key this machine presents will be trusted
Sign in with the account password
Import a server from a file
The file holds this app\'s SSH key for the server, the machines\' passwords, the pinned host keys and every password recorded here. Anyone who opens it can reach the server.
The server could not be moved
Show every section on this server
A section switched off the bar is still reachable inside a server, not lost.
Half-width cards carry fewer numbers and share a row with each other. This is the starting size and indicator for every server; a single card can change both from its own menu.

The server keeps running and its data is untouched — only the card, the app\'s SSH key and this server\'s pinned host keys are removed. To also clean up or wipe the machine, open the server and use \"Erase server\" on its management screen.
This removes everything gryonixNexus installed: containers, the reverse proxy, the tunnel, helper scripts and the app\'s own access — on every machine of this server.
Service data and backups stay on disk, so a later reinstall can pick them up.
Every service\'s data is deleted permanently. Backups are kept. This cannot be undone.
All backups on this server are deleted permanently. Live data is kept. This cannot be undone.
Every service\'s data AND all backups are deleted permanently, on every machine. There is no way back from this.
Every machine is clean. The card goes when this closes.
Nothing was removed from the list — the machine still has this app\'s access, so the job can be finished from here.
A group is a label on its servers. One with no servers left disappears.
Servers set up with this app appear here.
No services installed on this server.
Shows invented servers for screenshots. Nothing is written to your real fleet.
A single public machine runs everything.
A public relay in front, your own machine behind a tunnel.
No public names and no certificates from the internet.
No history on this machine yet.
The collector writes a row every ten seconds once the server has been set up by this app.
This machine reported nothing to show.

The script puts this device\'s key on the server, creates the account the app signs in as and adds the sudoers whitelist. Without it the scripts still install everything — the app just has no way in afterwards.
Watches this server\'s own logs for break-in attempts and blocks the IPs it catches. Off by choice only — leaving a server unwatched is what this question exists to ask about first.
It watches this server\'s own logs for break-in attempts and blocks the IPs it catches. Recommended for a server reachable from the internet.
The script neither creates it nor touches its key or password. The app signs in with the password below, which stays on this device.
The keystore refused to hand out a key, so the scripts grant no access.
The app connects over SSH, runs the scripts and shows live progress.
Run this once on the server, from the provider console or an SSH session you already have. It adds this device\'s key to the account you install as.
The address on your local network: the tunnel this run creates is not up yet.
The account that RUNS the script — usually root, never the account the script is about to create.
Answers, and it is the right distribution
The installation keeps running on the server; this only stops watching it.
The scripts are idempotent — a repeat run resumes at the machine that failed.
The script stopped because it could not see its A record yet. Add the records, wait for them to spread, and retry — or retry without the check if you know they are there.
Another service on this machine already holds a port this installation publishes. Retrying cannot help: free the port (or remove the service holding it) and start again.
It holds the passwords the server generated. It also stays on the server.
The rest of the install finished — these are non-fatal steps that did not, and can be fixed by re-running setup afterward.
To install from this device, turn on «Give this app access» above and generate again — the app needs an account and its key on the server.
This section is not built yet on Android.
The logic behind it is ported and tested; what is missing here is the screen.
Install a VPN protocol on one of your servers and its devices appear here — add a phone, hand it its configuration, take it away again.
These servers run a VPN, but the app cannot manage their devices: that goes through the server\'s own agent. Install the agent on the server, or open its VPN panel to add a device there.
These servers hand out VPN configurations from their own panel — that is how they are set up. Change it in the server\'s VPN settings to manage devices here as well.
Some of these hand out configurations from their own panel by choice; the rest have no agent installed for the app to go through.
No devices yet. Add one and the server hands back its configuration.
Its configuration stops working. This cannot be undone — a device added again is a new one, with a new address.
Add a server with the agent installed and everything it runs — what this app put there and what it did not — is listed here.
No agent on this server, so nothing can ask it what it runs. Install the agent to see and manage its containers.
The container engine did not answer

This group keeps nothing outside its images — no volume, no folder from the server and no database — so there is nothing a backup could have saved. Updating it pulls the newer images and starts them again; if that fails, the previous images are put back.
Every image is already the newest published.
The update failed and was rolled back: %1$s
The log could not be read
Working out what this would take…
Removing a line here means it is not archived. What can be listed is limited to what this server reported for this group.
These are dumped with their own client rather than copied from disk. A copy taken while the database is running restores into a broken one, and it does that without any error at the time.
The group is stopped while the archive is taken.
A database was found that cannot be dumped separately, so a consistent archive needs the stack stopped.
This plan was edited. Going back to detection lets the server work it out again from the images and mounts.
The server runs this on its own, so it does not need this device to be open.
With both off, the containers are stopped and removed and everything they held stays on the server.
These are named because the server refused to delete them, not because it forgot them.

An update can break a service. Before each one the server takes a backup, and if the service does not come back up it is rolled back to the image it was running. Configuration changes an update makes to its own data are not undone by that.
Backing up, then updating. This may take up to 10 minutes.
%1$s will be permanently deleted from the server.
Selected backups: %1$d. They will be permanently deleted from the server.
%1$s will be permanently deleted from the drive %2$s.
Selected backups: %1$d, including copies on USB drives. They will be permanently deleted.
Checking the size on the server…
This server cannot estimate the size. Re-run the installation to update its scripts.
The backup may not fit: it is larger than the free space on the server. A run that fills the disk takes the running services down with it.
This is a large backup. It can take a long time and will use as much disk space again while it runs.
Leave the password empty to use the one saved for scheduled backups. A password typed here is used only for this backup and is never stored — without it the archive cannot be decrypted.
The key this server already uses for its backups. Old and new archives open with the same password.
No key is saved on this server yet. Type a new password, or save one in Scheduled backups.
A password typed here is used only for these backups and is never stored — without it the archives cannot be decrypted.
The archive is written unencrypted. Encrypting a large library costs hours of processor time on a small server, which is why it is off here by default.
Restoring replaces this service\'s current data. Its containers go down while it runs, and running it again does not undo it.
The passphrase this archive was encrypted with. Without it the archive cannot be opened.
Choose the archive to restore from
Encrypted backups need this passphrase to run unattended. It is stored on the server, readable only by root, and you will need it to restore.
A passphrase is already stored on the server. Leave this empty to keep it.
A panel pins one machine, one set of metrics and one period, so several servers can be watched side by side. Add one to start the board.
Tap an account to publish with it; the pencil holds its two tokens. Records live on a zone and tunnels on the account, so the two need different permissions.
Devices are added on the server and appear in its VPN panel too — this is the same list, managed from the app.
CPU, memory and disk can be shown together — they share one 0 – 100 % axis. Anything else is plotted on its own.
Every device that joined this mesh. They reach each other directly, and this server relays only when a network refuses a direct connection.
%1$s leaves the mesh immediately. It can join again with a new key.
It is shown only now — the server does not hand it back.
Valid until %1$s. It is shown only now — the server does not hand it back.
Install the official Tailscale client, then run this. On a phone, use the app\'s “Use custom coordination server” option with the same address.
Makes this server\'s services reachable from your devices by their usual names, even where those names do not resolve publicly. The addresses stay private to the mesh.
No saved report yet. It is captured automatically when you install from this device; re-run the installation to fill it in.
No sign-in details in this report.
sshd is restarted on every machine of this server, one at a time: %1$s. Machines reached through another one go first.
The machine will go offline for about a minute while it restarts.
Reboot sent — the machine will be back in about a minute.
WireGuard only — other VPN protocols do not reach them

With this on, the admin panels answer only over the VPN; mail, user services and SSH stay public. WireGuard and AmneziaWG clients reach them; Shadowsocks and XRay carry internet traffic but never reach the panels. Create yourself a WireGuard client in the VPN panel and test it before switching this on.

Restricting the admin panels to VPN-only access needs a VPN installed on this server — the guard admits the tunnel\'s own subnet, so there would be nothing left to admit. Add a VPN protocol to this server and the switch appears here.
It is removed from the server. This cannot be undone from here — what comes back is whatever a backup holds.
A directory is only removed when it is empty; the server refuses otherwise, and says so.
%1$s is larger than the 200 MB a transfer is held in memory for, so it was not sent.
The device would not open the file you picked.
The VPN services share one panel, so they are removed together: %1$s.
VPN-only access ends with the VPN: these admin panels become reachable from the internet again — %1$s. Set a strong password on each before removing.
Containers and configuration are removed; data and backups stay on disk, so installing the service again can pick them up.
The service\'s data is deleted permanently. Its backups stay on disk. This cannot be undone.
Every backup of the service is deleted permanently. Its live data stays. This cannot be undone.
The service\'s data and every backup of it are deleted permanently. There is no way back from this.
The service and its data have been removed.
The service has been removed. Its data is still on the server.
The service is gone, but the host\'s management scripts could not be redrawn: %1$s
Every service this server can run is already installed.
The agent installs the service on the server. Its password ends up in the install report, like every other generated credential.
The server carries on if you close the app — the activity strip picks the run back up.
Each key is stored on the server, encrypted, and shared with your other devices. The gateway restarts by itself when a key changes.
A key is stored. Type a new one to replace it.
An empty field is left alone — only what you type is saved.
This server has no agent, so there is nowhere on it to store the keys. Put them in the file the install report names.
Encryption protects copies — a backup, a disk taken out of the machine. Anyone with root on this server can read the keys, because the gateway reads them too.
No models yet. Fetch one below — the engine is installed and empty.
The name is the one the model registry uses, tag included. The download runs on the server — you can close this screen.
No model engine is installed on this server.
Add Ollama to this server from the catalog, then come back.
This server has no agent, so the engine cannot be reached from here. Use the command the install report names.
Files you send up go straight into the server\'s mods directory and survive updates and changes to the catalogue. Restart the server from its card to load a new one.
Files you send up go straight into the server\'s plugins directory and survive updates and changes to the catalogue. Restart the server from its card to load a new one.
This server has no agent, so its files cannot be reached from here.
Only a .jar file can be uploaded here.
Each mailbox is an account on the mail server: the same address and password send and receive. The first one was created during the installation — its password is under Login & passwords.
Created outside the app — manage it on the server.
%1$s and every message in it are deleted from the server. This cannot be undone.
Latin letters, digits and . _ + - only — this is what the mail server accepts.
At least 8 characters. It goes to the server over the connection this app already holds and is stored only there — no copy is kept here, so write it down or copy it now.
The domain this token may edit.
One per line. Each must already exist as an A record.
A token scoped to edit DNS for this zone. It is stored on the server, readable only by root, and never sent back to this device.
The server holds a token. Leave this empty to keep it.
This server has no domain set, so its addresses cannot be built. Set it in Server settings — every service address is the service\'s own name plus that domain.
The key this server already uses signs in. Add it to the machine\'s authorized_keys first.
A machine is added only after it answers, so the server never holds one the app cannot reach.
This server signs in with a password, and this machine has its own account. It is kept on this device only.
Ask before writing a server to a file
Your fingerprint, face or device PIN guards these. A device with no lock set up is not asked — there would be nothing to ask with.
Nothing has been generated on this device yet.
The agent is not installed on this server.
The app sends the sources and the server builds them. The first build takes several minutes.
The server answers, but does not report a version.
Rebuilds gryonixnexusd %1$s on the server and restarts it. The agent stops answering for a few seconds; nothing else on the server is affected.

The private key is stored only in this device\'s keystore. The public key is added to servers by the setup scripts, or by hand to authorized_keys. The copied command authorizes the account you run it as — sudo in front is fine — and prints which account that was.
The old key will be deleted. The app will not be able to connect until the new public key is in authorized_keys on the servers.
The host key is remembered on the first connection. Reset it if the server was reinstalled — otherwise the connection will be rejected.
The next connection will trust whatever keys the servers present again.
There is nothing to export for this server: it publishes no DNS records, and no configuration for it was kept on this device.
The server configures its own firewall. This list is for the hoster\'s external firewall or security group.
Ports to open as a text list

Create it at Cloudflare with the Zone → DNS → Edit permission for your zone. It is kept behind this device\'s keystore and used only to write the records the configurator generates — always as \"DNS only\", never proxied.
Account-scoped, with Cloudflare Tunnel → Edit. The app uses it to create a tunnel and mint the connector\'s own credential, which is what makes cloudflared offerable at all.
Your own servers, set up for you
gryonixNexus writes the configuration, installs it over SSH and then manages it — mail, files, photos, passwords, VPN. No account, no cloud, nothing of yours passes through anybody else.
Pick what you want to run. The app generates the whole configuration — Docker, TLS, firewall, DNS records — and installs it on a machine you own.
Live CPU, memory, disk and traffic, backups on a schedule, updates with a rollback if the new image does not come up.
Credentials live in this device\'s keystore and on your server. There is no backend to trust, and no account to lose.
The servers you see behind this are examples, so every screen works before you own anything.

Add these to your DNS to finish setting up mail. Until they exist, outgoing mail is unsigned and most providers treat it as spam. Every other record was listed before the installation — this one the server had to generate first.
DKIM records as a BIND zone file
Most DNS providers can import the zone file or the CSV directly, so the records need not be typed in by hand.
The key is not ready yet. The mail engine generates it shortly after its first start.
Opens the configurator filled in from this server. Running it again targets this same machine.
Kept on this device only, for this machine. The app never uses it for anything else.
Sign in with the key this app already uses
No servers yet. A shell is opened on a machine this app knows.
On the local server at home
A model engine is installed on this server. Without a graphics card a small model answers at a few words a second, and each model is 4–40 GB of disk.
The engine goes on the machine at home, where a graphics card can do the work; this server only relays.
Nothing runs here. The chat calls a provider you have an API key for, and every message leaves the server.

The install adds NVIDIA\'s container toolkit and restarts docker once — every container on that server restarts with it. The DRIVER is not installed: if the machine has none, the engine runs on the processor and the report says so.
The engine runs on the processor. On a server without a graphics card that is a few words a second for a small model.
The catalog will not build a game server whose license is unaccepted — it would exit on every start.
I accept Mojang\'s End User License Agreement (Java)
I accept Mojang\'s End User License Agreement (Bedrock)
This machine stands in my home
Switch on what this server should run. Where a shelf holds several products, tap it to choose which one.
Each protocol has its own port and its own client app; any number can run side by side. The panel that hands out client configurations comes with them.
The domain name your services will use, e.g. example.com. You can add more — every service answers on all of them, and with mail each gets its own mailboxes.
The public IP address of your server.
The public IP address of your VPS. The local server\'s address on your network is entered later, during installation.
A LAN IP address or a .local hostname your devices can already reach — not a domain you\'d register (like example.com). This is both the server\'s address and its Caddy site name, self-signed.
The login the services that share one administrator account are created with. The password is generated on the server and written into the install report.
Create these records at your registrar before installing — a certificate cannot be issued for a name that does not resolve yet. The exact list is generated with the files.
Add these records at your domain provider. Until they exist and have spread, nothing on your domain will work.
Create them once. This server then keeps them pointing at its current address by itself — switch that on from the server\'s own screen after the install, with a provider token.
Fill in the domain and the server address to see the exact records.

Cloudflare: DNS → Records → “Import and Export” → “Import DNS records” → upload the zone file (Cloudflare accepts only that one, not the CSV). Then set every record to “DNS only” (grey cloud) — the orange cloud breaks mail and the VPN. The CSV is for panels that import a spreadsheet instead.

Create the token at Cloudflare with the Zone → DNS → Edit permission for your zone. It is stored on this device and used only to write the records above. Records are created as “DNS only”, never proxied.
The provider the Configurator\'s own publish step opens on. It can still be switched there for one publish.
Create the token under API → Tokens/Keys with read and write scope. It is stored on this device and used only to write the records above.
Create the token in the DNS console under API Tokens. It is stored on this device and used only to write the records above.

Create an API key under Account → API Access, and enable API access for this domain in its Domain Management page. Porkbun needs both the API key and the secret key — paste them here together, separated by a colon: apikey:secretapikey. Stored on this device and used only to write the records above.

Create a token at api.ovh.com/createToken with the rights GET/POST/PUT on /domain/zone/*. OVH gives you three keys — application key, application secret and consumer key — paste all three here, separated by colons: applicationKey:applicationSecret:consumerKey. Uses the EU endpoint (eu.api.ovh.com). Stored on this device and used only to write the records above.

Create an IAM user with the AmazonRoute53FullAccess policy (or a custom policy scoped to your hosted zone) and an access key for it. Paste the access key ID and the secret access key here together, separated by a colon: accessKeyID:secretAccessKey. Stored on this device and used only to write the records above.

Create a service account with the DNS Administrator role, then create a JSON key for it and paste the WHOLE downloaded file here — client email, private key and project id all travel together in that one file. Stored on this device and used only to write the records above.
Create a Personal Access Token from the GoDaddy Developer dashboard. Stored on this device and used only to write the records above.
Generating writes the setup scripts and the DNS records for exactly these answers. Nothing is sent anywhere and nothing runs on a server until you install.
GitLab needs about 8 GB of memory — tap to pick Forgejo instead.
Ollama runs models but has no web page of its own. Add Open WebUI to chat with them from a browser.
Needs about 8 GB of memory on its own and several minutes for its first start. Forgejo is the same git hosting on a fraction of that.
Works from anywhere: it serves the filter over DNS-over-HTTPS through the same HTTPS name as its panel.
Serves plain DNS only — right for a machine on your own network, which your router points at. Devices elsewhere need AdGuard Home instead.
Paints the app\'s buttons, switches and highlights. Delete and erase stay red whatever is chosen here.

The server screen lists every installed service\'s web address. With a full catalog that is a dozen links pushing the rest of the screen down — the first switch lets that section be folded away. Grouping files installed services under their category (Files, Media, VPN, …) instead of listing them one by one; on Automatic it turns itself on for a server that runs two or more services of the same kind, which is when a category header actually shortens the list.

Inline unfolds the history chart under the host instead of opening a separate screen. Auto fits the chart scale to the data, so small variations stay visible. 0–100% keeps the absolute scale, which is what compares two machines by glance.
The periods on the strip under a chart, and the metrics in its menu. Nothing about how they are measured changes — this only decides what you are offered. At least one of each always stays on.
Buttons answer a press with a short tap.

CrowdSec watches this server\'s login and web logs and automatically blocks the addresses behind repeated attacks — brute-force, scanning, known-bad hosts. It\'s installed and kept up to date with the server, and enforces a blocklist shared by every CrowdSec install. There\'s nothing to configure.
This server\'s intrusion defence could not be reached — it may not be installed, or the agent may be too old to report it. Install it here, re-run setup, or update the agent.

CrowdSec and its firewall bouncer are uninstalled from this server, and the addresses it is blocking right now are released with them. Nothing else on the server is touched. It can be installed again here.

This server stops watching its login and web logs, and the addresses it is blocking are released. Attacks are not blocked until it is started again — which does happen on the next restart of the machine, because the service stays enabled.

This server will only accept SSH key logins. This app\'s key is on %1$s, and it stays — but anyone who signs in to this machine with a password, including you from a console or another computer, will not be able to any more. It can be turned back on here.
Passwords are what automated attacks try, thousands of times a day. Turn this back on only if you need to sign in to this machine without a key.
Whether this server accepts SSH passwords is read from the machine itself.
This server did not say what its SSH accepts, so nothing is offered here. The agent may be too old for it, or the machine may have no sshd of its own.

The setting that closes password login is on this server and sshd is ignoring it — something earlier in its SSH configuration allows passwords, usually a cloud image\'s own file in /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d. It has to be removed on the machine.
This server accepts SSH keys only. The app signs in with the key it keeps on this device.

This server still accepts SSH passwords, which is what automated attacks try. Password login can only be turned off once this app can get in without one — adding the key does that, over the connection the app already has, and switches this server to key sign-in.
This server still accepts SSH passwords. Turning that off leaves SSH keys as the only way in — this app\'s key is already on %1$s, and the setting can be turned back on here.
Kept on the server — these are the same on every device paired with it.
Saved on this device only. Install the agent on this server to share them with your other devices.
This device has been signed out of the server, so its saved passwords were cleared. Open Paired Devices to sign in again.
The server will not answer this device, because it cannot say which device it is. Nothing was cleared: for now these values are local to this device.
Saved on this device. The server could not be reached, so your other devices will see this after the next sync.
Removing a device takes it out of this list. It does NOT revoke its SSH access — its key keeps working until it is removed from the server separately.
No devices are paired with this server yet.
%1$s is removed from the server\'s paired-device list. This does NOT revoke its SSH access — its key keeps working until it is removed from the server separately.
Past this the server stops answering a device until it pairs again. It does not touch SSH access.
This device cannot tell the server which device it is, so the server refuses every request. This is not the session timer, and signing in again will not help.
Confirm your identity with biometrics or your device PIN to sign in again.
Kept in %1$s. Restoring one is not offered here yet — putting a stranger\'s volumes back over a running stack is a step this app does not take without proving it on a real server first.
Restoring one is not offered here yet — putting a stranger\'s volumes back over a running stack is a step this app does not take without proving it on a real server first.
The path survives a reboot only under /dev/serial/by-id — a plain /dev/ttyUSB0 can point at a different stick after the next start.
Read the sticks off the server
The server sees no stick plugged in. Plug it in and read the list again.
This machine has never had a USB serial adapter — there is nothing to pick yet.
This server has no agent to ask.
The server could not be read.
Its phone app signs in with its own account and cannot pass this login — the app stops connecting, the website keeps working.
Turn on the services you want behind one login — they will appear here.
Serve DNS to the local network
Port 53 is published on every interface. Only do this where it cannot be reached from the internet — an open resolver is abused for amplification attacks within days.
DNS answers on this machine only. Devices on your network cannot use the filter until you turn this on.
With no whitelist, anyone who knows the address can join.
Mojang ships this server for x86 only. On an ARM machine it runs under emulation and is noticeably slower.
Addresses inside the WireGuard tunnel between the VPS and the local server.

Version %1$s. gryonixNexus is installed from a file, so it asks gryonix.com whether a newer one has been published — no identifier, no data about your servers. The download opens in your browser; installing it stays with you and Android.
Unlock to sign this device in to the server
The mailbox password was changed, but could not be saved to the shared password vault. Keep your copy of the new password.
Tap a token to publish with it; the pencil holds the token itself, the name and which provider it belongs to.
No DNS token yet. Add one to publish the generated records straight into your zone instead of exporting a zone file and importing it by hand.
Wake-up sent from this device to %1$s.
This device could not send the packet.
The machine has not reported its network card yet. Open this server once while it is on.
This machine\'s network card cannot wake it up, for example over Wi-Fi.
Nothing is blocked by this server right now.
This server\'s CrowdSec is too old to keep an allowlist. Updating the protection adds it.
%1$s can reach this server again. It will be blocked again if it repeats what it was blocked for — protect it to stop that.
Every connection from this address is dropped until the block expires.
This address is never blocked, whatever it does. Protect the network you administer the server from — once blocked, it cannot be released from there.
Needs a login that can run useradd — root, or an account with full sudo.
Lower-case letters, digits, - and _; must start with a letter. Names the system already uses are refused.
The account gets a home directory, a shell, and this app\'s public key — so you can sign in to it from the terminal straight away.
Runs over SSH as the account this app signs in with. It needs root, or full sudo — a management user created by an install does not have it.
Created “%1$s”. Add it as a login above.
Notifications, permissions and battery treatment for this app — the settings the phone owns rather than the app.
These apply to this device only. A server exported to another device does not carry them — a jump host or a wake-up address is a fact about the network you reach it from.

Every connection to this server is made through the machine chosen here — the way in when the server itself is not reachable from the internet, or when only one machine is allowed to reach it. Nothing is stored on the server; this is the route this device takes.
A server this app already manages needs no address, account or key typed here — it has all three, and they stay right when the server changes.
A jump box this app does not manage. It signs in with this device\'s own key, which has to be authorized on that host the same way it is on a server.
A fallback with no address and no bastion would retry exactly what just failed.

Tried automatically when the server\'s usual address does not answer. Leave Host empty to retry the same address through the bastion chosen here. This is about reaching the machine — the copies of its data are a different screen, under Backups.
Not available in this build — the app\'s SSH library has no agent channel, and a phone runs no agent to forward.

A backup that lives on the machine it was taken from does not survive that machine — which is the one failure a backup is for. Copies are sent right after each archive is made, by the same schedule that makes them. A copy that fails never fails the backup; it is recorded here instead.
Picking one fills in its address and account. The key the copies travel with is made by THIS server; only its public half ever leaves it.
This server\'s own name is added to the folder, so several servers can share one destination without landing on each other.

Any S3-compatible storage. The credentials are written to a root-only file on the server and never read back — leave the field empty to keep what is already stored. The server needs rclone installed; the check below says so if it is missing.

A scan arrives from a hoster\'s range rather than from one address, so blocking the address it used this minute is work the next minute undoes — the neighbourhood is the /24 around it. Blocking a whole range also catches machines that have done nothing, which is the price.
A wrong password on SSH is a break-in attempt; a wrong password on a web form is Tuesday. Name the service as the protection names it — ssh, http, smtp.

A proxy carries the connection to a server for you — the answer when this network refuses direct connections outright. A server picks one in its own settings, under Advanced. It is not a bastion: a bastion is a machine that connects onward on your behalf, and where both are set the proxy is dialled first.
SOCKS5 carries any connection and is what a phone or a router usually offers. HTTP CONNECT is what a company\'s web proxy offers; it carries the same bytes through a different greeting.
